samples.summary: Cleared ('') marker color short-circuits the `??` fallback, so the list marker paints the theme default instead of inheriting the inline's color
samples.evidence: `const colorSource = m?.color ?? firstInline?.color;` — the whole premise of this change is that `''` means "unset" (see `isEmptyStoredColor`, `resolveStoredColor`). But `??` only falls through on `null`/`undefined`, so a marker whose color was cleared to `''` never consults `firstInline?.color`; `resolveStoredColor` then maps `''` → undefined and line 555 paints `theme.defaultColor`. A marker with NO color at all correctly inherits the inline's `#FF9900`, while a marker whose color was cleared does not — two spellings of the same state behave differently. The normalization has to happen before the `??` chain (e.g. `const colorSource = (isEmpty(m?.color) ? undefined : m?.color) ?? firstInline?.color`). The new test in packages/docs/test/view/render-list-marker.test.ts ('paints an empty-string marker color with the theme default') pins the inconsistent behavior in place.

samples.summary: The new slides-arm block walker validates block styles but not inline entries, so a PUT can still store a slide text block whose `inlines[i].text` is missing/non-string — which throws inside the docs layout engine for every viewer
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` (controller.ts:683-720) checks only `block.style` and recurses into `tableData`. The docs arm added exactly the opposite guard for the same `Block` shape — 'buildInlineNode reads inline.text.length … an element missing either turns a malformed PUT into a 500' (controller.ts:422-442). Slide text bodies are persisted verbatim as JSON by `writeSlidesRoot`, then laid out by the SAME docs engine: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:286` does `const len = inline.text.length` and 289/290 `inline.text.slice(...)`. A payload of `{slides:[{…,elements:[{id,type:'text',frame:{},data:{blocks:[{style:{},inlines:[{}]}]}}]}]}` is accepted, and thereafter `computeLayout` throws a TypeError on every render of that slide (all viewers), not just a 400 for the caller. The stated round-trip rationale only justifies tolerating *omitted* `id`/`inlines`, not an inline entry with a non-string `text`.

samples.summary: New inline guard checks `style` is an object but not `style.image`, and `serializeInlineStyle` dereferences `style.image.src` unconditionally → 500 on `{image: null}`
samples.evidence: The guard's own comment says its job is that 'an element missing either turns a malformed PUT into a 500 from inside the writer'. But packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:89-92 does `if (style.image !== undefined) { attrs['image.src'] = style.image.src; … }` — a payload with `inlines:[{text:'x',style:{image:null}}]` passes the new validation (`style` is an object) and then throws a TypeError inside `buildTreeChildren`, producing the same 500 the guard was added to prevent. (No data loss: `buildTreeChildren` runs before any tree mutation.)

samples.summary: `header.marginFromEdge: null` is rejected with a 400 while every other new numeric check in the same change treats `null` as absent
samples.evidence: `if (r.marginFromEdge !== undefined && (typeof r.marginFromEdge !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(...)))` — `null !== undefined`, so `{header:{blocks:[],marginFromEdge:null}}` 400s. This contradicts `assertValidBlockStyle` two functions below (`if (value === undefined || value === null) continue;`, with the doc comment 'null is treated as absent for every field … how JSON spells "no value"') and contradicts the writer it is protecting: `serializeMarginFromEdgeAttrs` explicitly handles `marginFromEdge === null` by emitting no attribute (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:110). A caller clearing the margin with JSON `null` gets a 400 for a value the writer would happily drop.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` does not recognise `#RGBA` shorthand or the space-separated / percentage `rgb()` forms, so those colors are now silently dropped at every OOXML sink and painted black in PDF
samples.evidence: The regex `^rgba?\(\s*([-+\d.]+)\s*,...` only accepts comma-separated numeric channels, and the hex branches accept 3/6/8 digits but not 4 (`#f00f` = opaque red in CSS). Every export sink was just routed through this single function (docx-style-map.ts:95/99, docx-exporter.ts cell fill, pptx text.ts `storedColorToThemeColor`, pdf-style-map.ts:152), so any color stored in one of those shapes — legal CSS that the canvas paints correctly on screen — now exports as 'no color' (DOCX/PPTX) or black (PDF), a visible screen-vs-export divergence. `rgb(0 128 255 / 50%)` and `rgb(100%, 0%, 0%)` fall in the same hole.

samples.summary: `applyBlockStyle` has no attribute-removal counterpart, so a block-style key merged in as explicitly `undefined` now leaves the stale CRDT attribute behind while the local cache shows it cleared
samples.evidence: `const merged = normalizeBlockStyle({ ...block.style, ...style }); const attrs = serializeBlockStyle(merged);` then `tree.styleByPath(blockPath, attrs)` with no `removeNodeStyle`. `normalizeBlockStyle` is `{...DEFAULT, ...style}`, so an own key valued `undefined` survives the spread, and the new `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` skips it (`if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue`) — `styleByPath` only merges, so the previous attribute stays on the node while line 1519 sets `block.style = merged` in the cache. The cache and the CRDT then disagree until reload. The inline (`removedInlineStyleAttrs`) and cell (`removedCellStyleAttrs`) paths both got exactly this treatment in this change; the block path did not. I found no current caller passing an explicit `undefined` block-style value, hence low confidence.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: the slides walker `assertValidSlideBlocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:683-720) validates only `block.style` and recurses into `tableData`; it never inspects `block.inlines`, while the docs arm for the same Block shape rejects non-string `inline.text` and missing `inline.style` (:419-442). I searched wide for a compensating normalizer and found none: `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:93-110) stores verbatim; `migrateDocument`/`migrateSlide`/`migrateElement` (slides/model/migrate.ts:68-168) never touch blocks/inlines; `ensureSlidesRoot` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:283-296) only repairs non-array blocks/notes; the slides renderer normalizes only block style (text-renderer.ts:256-266 via normalizeBlockStyle, docs/model/types.ts:272-274); and the emptiness short-circuit `isBlocksEmpty` (slides/model/element.ts:651-656) tests `inline.text === ''`, so `{}` counts as non-empty and reaches layout. The docs layout engine then dereferences it unguarded: measureSegments reads `inline.text.length` (docs/view/layout.ts:785) and `splitWords(inline.text)` (:794), and splitWords immediately does `text.length` (:841-842) -> TypeError. A malformed PUT is therefore persisted and crashes rendering for every viewer of that deck, a missing-guard/stored-crash bug squarely in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Slides text-body style validation is stricter than the slides reader, so a GET → edit → PUT round-trip of an existing deck can now 400
finding.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` calls `assertValidBlockStyle` (line 602), which throws on any present style value that is not a finite number (`value !== undefined && (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value))`, controller line 329-336) — so `lineHeight: null`, `marginTop: null`, or an alignment outside `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` is a 400. Unlike the docs arm, slide text bodies are persisted and returned VERBATIM (`writeSlidesRoot`/`readSlidesRoot` store plain JSON; the comment at line 570-576 states this explicitly and deliberately relaxes only the *structural* checks). Consequently a deck already holding such a value is readable through GET but no longer writable through PUT — the CLI read-modify-write flow breaks on data the caller never touched. The docs arm avoids this because `parseBlockStyleAttrs` drops the same values on read; the slides arm has no such normalizer. Either normalize on the slides read path or make the slides style check drop-and-continue instead of throwing.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. (1) The quoted predicate `value !== undefined && (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value))` does not exist; the actual numeric loop is `if (value === undefined || value === null) continue;` (docs-content.controller.ts:351) before the finite-number check at :352, so `lineHeight: null` / `marginTop: null` pass validation rather than 400. (2) The alignment check is parameterized: `assertValidBlockStyle(style, path, alignmentRule = 'allowlist')` (:330-348) only applies the `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` allowlist when the rule is 'allowlist' (used by the docs arm at :374); the slides arm passes `'string'` (`assertValidSlideBlocks` -> :698-702), which accepts any string alignment, and skips null/undefined at :336. Slide `notes` go through the same relaxed path (:557). The comment block at :314-328 documents both tolerances as deliberately added for exactly the GET->edit->PUT round-trip concern the finding raises. Both concrete 400 vectors named in the finding therefore do not fire; the described stricter-than-reader behavior is not present.

finding.summary: Group children are now validated with the full `assertValidElement`, which can reject decks that previously round-tripped
finding.evidence: `assertValidElement` now recurses into `data.children` (line 550-555) and applies the full element contract — non-empty `id` (line 509) and an object `frame` (line 519) — to nested elements that were never validated before. Group children are persisted verbatim as JSON with no reader-side normalization, so any legacy/imported group child missing `id` or `frame` turns a previously-accepted PUT into a 400, breaking GET → edit → PUT for that deck. The docs arm sidesteps this only because `readDocsRoot` synthesizes the fields it demands; nothing does that for slides.

verdict.reason: The finding claims group children are validated with the full `assertValidElement` (requiring non-empty `id` and object `frame`), causing 400s on GET→edit→PUT of legacy decks. The code does the opposite. `assertValidElementData`'s group branch (docs-content.controller.ts:636-641) dispatches each child to `assertValidNestedElement` (line 639), not `assertValidElement`. `assertValidNestedElement` (lines 595-600) is deliberately identity-free: it only requires the child be an object and then walks its text bodies via `assertValidElementData` — no `id` check, no `frame` check. Its doc comment (lines 583-594) explicitly names and avoids the exact round-trip regression the finding describes, as does the layout usage at line 513. `assertValidElement` (lines 560-581) is invoked only from the slide's own `elements` loop (line 553) and does not recurse into `data.children` itself. The repo's tests pin this: docs-content.controller.spec.ts:872 is `'accepts a group child that omits id and frame'`, and :858-869 shows only a bad block style inside a child is rejected. The evidence's cited line numbers (550-555 for the children recursion, 509 for the id check, 519 for the frame check) also do not match the file — those lines are the slide elements loop, the layout array guard, and the `assertValidSlide` object check respectively.
